newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil slides to match crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil slides to match crude.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil prices slipped on Monday, in line with last Friday's late fall in Brent crude values, traders said.
Business was thin with offers of around $97 heard and no cargo bids seen.
There was no U.S. interest reported. One 5,000 tonne barge trade was heard done on mainland Europe at $100 fob.
"Its a terrible picture for straight-run at the moment," said one seller.
Most players were content to wait to see if crude prices stabilise.
Refinery buyers in the Mediterranean were said to be ignoring straight-run in favour of crude, which offers substantially higher margins.
"It is very unhealthy for any resid as refineries don't want it, people are flat out on crude," said one broker.

A cargo of Russian low sulphur loading 9-10 April was heard bought at high cif quotes plus $1. Another cargo which loaded at the weekend had been placed and a third, also loading 9-10 April was being discussed today, traders said.
Activity in the high sulphur straight-run market in the Mediterranean was also said to be easing off. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
